clue.text: Scientific study exposed trope in collection of writings

indicators.note: in says the stripped trope goes inside the collection word

parts.note: an anthology is a collection of pieces of writing

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: the middle three letters of trope

explanation.surface: Research lays bare a figure of speech in a literary anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' means its covering removed, so a word loses its outer letters; 'in' then splits the collection of writings after its fourth letter to take them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the scientific study of humankind and its cultures and societies.

clue.text: Mix up the order of a couple of farm animals

definitions.note: the definition describes what an anagram is, a mixing up of the order of letters

parts.note: two farm animals: a nag, an old horse, and a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer shuffles a pair of livestock into a different line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like an anagram instruction but describes the answer instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word made by rearranging the letters of another, so it is a mixing of their sequence.

clue.text: Danced tango with one short step close to end

parts.note: tango is T in the radio alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the last letter goes
the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of end

explanation.surface: A ballroom dancer took a tango step shortened at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' looks like the dance but is the radio-alphabet letter. 'short' trims STEP to STE.
explanation.definitionFit: The twist is a 1960s dance, so twisted is a past tense meaning did that dance.

clue.text: Complicated instructions fix morale somehow

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly, as in rigging an election

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of morale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Convoluted orders are meant to repair low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, complicated procedure or set of directions.

clue.text: Beat some impulses

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a part of the next word

parts.note: letters two to six of impulses

explanation.surface: A drumbeat arising from a few sudden urges.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside im-PULSE-s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a regular beat, such as the throb of the heart.

clue.text: Coherent American soldier in pub

indicators.note: in says the soldier goes inside the pub word

parts.note: the local is a regular's nearby pub
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman in a bar is still speaking clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A logical argument is coherent: it follows reason and holds together.

clue.text: Info on Morecambe perhaps is widely applicable

indicators.note: on says one piece is placed above the other in this down clue

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so his first name is Eric

explanation.surface: Facts about a famous comic turn out to be universally relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a seaside town, but here the comedian of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, relating to a whole class rather than one item, so broadly applicable.

clue.text: Angrily he cut erratic style of building

indicators.note: angrily suggests violent upheaval, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A furious builder snips away at a wayward design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'Angrily' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture means a particular design or manner of construction, such as Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Interpret writing in grand county town

parts.note: to read is to interpret writing
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone deciphers a document in a fine English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the county town of Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is the administrative centre of the English county of Berkshire, a county town.

clue.text: Traditional tales of feet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: traditional stories handed down
second meaning: the feet are at the ends of the legs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: split the answer as LEG ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends are old stories passed down, and split in two the word describes where feet are found.

clue.text: Dreadful fiascos taint feeling of contentment

indicators.note: dreadful means very bad, so the letters are in a terrible mess and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Awful blunders spoil one's sense of being pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the pleasure felt when a wish is fulfilled, a sense of being content.

clue.text: Infusion starts to help even reluctant believers treat extreme anxiety

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.words: help even reluctant believers treat extreme anxiety
parts.note: the first letter of each of these seven words

explanation.surface: A calming drink is said to help sceptics with severe stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first letter of each word from 'help' to 'anxiety'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb tea is made by steeping herbs in hot water, which is what an infusion is.

clue.text: Crept around following old passage

indicators.note: following says the rearranged letters come after the old word

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: around means in a different arrangement, so the letters of crept are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked about after a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal, but nothing is contained: it reorders CREPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Tiny boy with papers is shy

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A little lad holding his documents is bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' looks descriptive, but it is part of the name Tiny Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means lacking courage or confidence, much like shy.

clue.text: Pollution spoils lickspittle's trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the last four letters of spoils and the first five of lickspittle

explanation.surface: A grovelling flatterer's trousers are ruined by dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb, meaning pockets: sp-OILS LICKS-pittle holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil slicks are films of spilt oil on the sea, a familiar form of pollution.

clue.text: Meal including starter of appetising stuff is a good place to start

indicators.note: including says the meal word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of appetising
to pad is to stuff, as with padding

explanation.surface: A meal with a tasty first course is a fine way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it means the first letter, A, which goes inside LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch pad is the platform rockets lift off from, so figuratively a springboard for a venture.

clue.text: Dissolve cure into a drink

indicators.note: to dissolve something is to break it up, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Stir a remedy into a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a drink.

clue.text: I mostly speak in a fancy language

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to talk is to speak

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imagined, so the letters of in a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast of speaking mostly in an elaborate way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TALK to TAL, and 'fancy' turns IN A into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the language of Italy, a Romance tongue.

clue.text: Little European swimmer

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a Pole is a European, from Poland

explanation.surface: A small continental competing in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a human athlete, but the swimmer is a young frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larva of a frog or toad, which lives in water and swims.

clue.text: Show Alexandra making sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the words hold the answer inside

parts.note: the last three letters of Alexandra and the first two of making

explanation.surface: A woman called Alexandra prepares sandwiches for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making sandwiches' looks like food, but 'sandwiches' is a verb: alexan-DRA MA-king.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a show performed on stage or screen.

clue.text: Couturier leads a Master of Arts display

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so the designer comes first

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous French couturier, a fashion designer
MA is the degree abbreviation for Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A fashion house heads a graduate's exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model scene, often in a museum display case.

clue.text: Two articles about hired sportswoman

indicators.note: about says the two articles go around the hired word

parts.note: two articles: the indefinite a and the definite the
let means hired out, as a flat is let

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces about a sportswoman who was signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: A and THE are split by LET.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, here a woman.

clue.text: Without help, Auden and I'd improvised

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: The poet W H Auden and the speaker made things up with no assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided means done alone, with no assistance from anyone else.

clue.text: Ideal doctor introduces drug in the morning

indicators.note: introduces means comes in front of, so the doctor comes first

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
AM is the abbreviation for the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A doctor brings in a new medicine first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is something perfect one longs for, such as a dream home, so an ideal.

clue.text: Note, less time for needlework

indicators.note: less means without, so the time letter is taken out

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

explanation.surface: A note asks for less time to be spent on sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is the British name for a quarter note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is a craft of making fabric from yarn with a hooked needle.

clue.text: Typical example of endless long story, in my opinion

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic story
to me means in my opinion, as in 'to me, it's wrong'

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a never-ending saga is a model case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts EPIC to EPI. A tome is a big book, but here the letters come from TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example of a type, such as the epitome of elegance.

clue.text: It has no effect when piano string breaks off at first

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a lace is a string, as in a shoelace

indicators.note: at first means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of breaks and off

explanation.surface: A piano string snapping leaves the sound unaffected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks off' looks like the string snapping, but 'at first' takes B and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, given to compare against a real drug.

clue.text: During time at school Ed and I dined between others

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is a period of the school year
ate means dined

explanation.surface: During a school term, Ed and the speaker ate in the middle of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediate means coming between two other things in position or level.
